title: Search Autocomplete: Complete Architecture
description: Design a search autocomplete system with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a search autocomplete system that provides instant prefix-based suggestions as users type in a search box. The system must handle billions of queries per day, support typo tolerance, rank suggestions by popularity and relevance, serve results from edge caches in under 50 milliseconds, and update its index in near real-time as new content is published or trending topics emerge.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Return up to 10 suggestions matching the current query prefix
Support fuzzy matching to correct typos and misspellings
Rank suggestions by query frequency, recency, and personalization signals
Categorize suggestions (products, categories, brands, people, locations)
Show result counts or preview thumbnails alongside suggestions
Support trending and recently searched queries per user or globally
Highlight the matched portion of each suggestion in the UI
Allow keyboard navigation through suggestion list (arrow keys, enter)
Debounce input on the client to reduce API load during fast typing

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Sub-50ms p99 response time for suggestion API from edge cache
99.99% availability; suggestions must remain available even if indexing fails
Handle 100,000 queries per second globally during peak traffic
Index updates visible to users within 30 seconds of content creation
Memory-efficient trie or prefix index for tens of millions of unique queries
Graceful degradation: fallback to popular queries when cache is cold
Geographically distributed for low latency across continents
Analytics pipeline records query volume, zero-result queries, and click-through rates

data.text: Start with a monolithic ASP.NET Core API that loads a compressed prefix trie or a search index into memory at startup. The service exposes a single /suggestions endpoint that accepts a query prefix, traverses the trie, applies ranking heuristics, and returns ranked suggestions. This is the fastest way to validate search relevance, typo tolerance, and ranking logic before moving to a distributed architecture.

data.title: Monolith Tech Stack
data.code:
Frontend:
  - React 18 with TypeScript
  - Vite for build tooling
  - Tailwind CSS for styling
  - React Query for server state

Backend (ASP.NET Core):
  - Minimal API or MVC Controllers
  - Entity Framework Core for data access
  - Azure SQL Database or AWS RDS for relational data
  - Built-in DI, logging, and health checks

Infrastructure:
  - Azure App Service or AWS EC2/ECS
  - Azure Blob Storage or AWS S3 for file assets
  - Azure Monitor or AWS CloudWatch for logging
  - Single database with tables for all domains

data.text: At scale, split into microservices for independent indexing, ranking, and serving. Crawler Service discovers new content from data sources. Indexer Service builds and updates a compact prefix index or trie with frequency and metadata. Search Service serves suggestions from a distributed cache with fallback to a search engine. Ranking Service reorders suggestions using ML models trained on click data. Query Analyzer normalizes inputs and detects trending topics.

items: Crawler Service: Discovers new content from databases, websites, or product catalogs and emits IndexUpdate events to refresh the suggestion index.
Indexer Service: Builds and maintains a compact prefix trie or search index with term frequencies, categories, and metadata; publishes index snapshots to distributed storage.
Search Service: Serves suggestions from an in-memory cache or search engine like Elasticsearch or Redis; applies prefix matching and falls back to popular terms on cache miss.
Ranking Service: Reorders raw suggestions using ML models trained on historical click-through rates, user context, and freshness signals.
Query Analyzer: Normalizes query strings (lowercasing, stemming, typo correction), detects trending queries, and routes personalized requests to the ranking layer.
Snippet Service: Fetches preview metadata like product images, category labels, and result counts to enrich suggestion items in the UI.

Key Patterns:
  - Feature-based folder structure
  - API Gateway as single entry point
  - React Query for caching and background refetch
  - WebSocket / SSE for real-time updates
  - Error boundaries and retry logic

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: A Search Autocomplete system requires both simple and scalable designs
Monolith is fastest to validate; microservices are for scale
React + ASP.NET Core provides a robust full-stack foundation
Azure Cosmos DB and Amazon DynamoDB are strong choices for distributed data
Always design for failure: retries, circuit breakers, and fallbacks
data.takeaway: Search Autocomplete is a distributed system. Start simple, then scale horizontally with microservices, caching, and managed cloud services.
